description:
Trigger: finding_seed (oscal/emit.rs:776-793), risk_seed (797-807), subject_seed (811-816), and the EvidenceKey::seed implementations write the cert_index / position-index value via usize::to_le_bytes(). usize is 8 bytes on 64-bit targets and 4 bytes on 32-bit targets.

Actual bad behavior: an OSCAL evaluation report emitted on a 32-bit host produces different Observation / Finding / Risk UUIDs from the same logical inputs evaluated on a 64-bit host. Evidence-pack provenance is documented as deterministic ('Two Findings with identical (cert_sha256, cert_index) produce the same...' at oscal/emit.rs:226-228) but the determinism only holds within a single target architecture.

Not a security exploit, but it undermines the documented provenance binding. A consumer who replays a report's UUIDs on a different host arch sees mismatches. CT/audit workflows that compare reports across infrastructure with mixed arch will silently disagree.

Section G — 'parameters are explicit; deterministic nonce → derivation function and collision argument' applies to the seed construction. The fix is trivially mechanical and tracks the workspace's overall portability stance.

Fix: replace every usize::to_le_bytes() in the seed builders with (value as u64).to_le_bytes(). The seed length grows by 4 bytes per index field on 32-bit; UUIDs change once (a breaking provenance change) and become portable thereafter.

Affected functions:
- report_seed (chain_length is already u64-ish via the .to_le_bytes() on a u64-typed field — verify)
- finding_seed (uses i: usize → to_le_bytes; uses cert_index: Option<usize>)
- risk_seed (uses i: usize → to_le_bytes)
- subject_seed (uses cert_index: usize → to_le_bytes)
- EvidenceKey::seed (oscal/emit.rs:226-247, check the cert_index serialization)

Section: G (algorithm and parameter choice — deterministic derivation must be platform-portable)
title: UUIDv8 seeds use usize::to_le_bytes — UUIDs are non-portable across 32-bit vs 64-bit hosts
